title: E06 re-run on multi-file tasks: does a repo graph beat lexical search where the answer spans modules?
hypothesis: The dev-suite E06 run put graph-only exposure 38% more expensive than lexical with equal quality, but every dev task lives in one file, so a graph had nothing to traverse. On two frozen tasks whose fix spans five modules, graph-only is non-inferior in quality and not more expensive than lexical.

task_cluster_definition.cluster: one task is one cluster; both tasks require locating code across modules
task_cluster_definition.dev_suite_note: already consumed by the E06 dev run; not reused here
task_cluster_definition.fairness_check: each task graded unsolved (exit 1) and with a reference solution (exit 0) before the run
task_cluster_definition.third_arm: graph+history is not expressible: code_graph takes query/focus_files/max_nodes and has no history mode
task_cluster_definition.pre_run_correction: the first frozen form put a [path, content] pair in expect_absent, which the suite schema rejects (it takes paths only); the assertion was redundant with the oracle test, so it was dropped and the hash re-frozen before any run

model_identity_observability.note: same model both arms; absolute token claims carry the model identity

quality_margin.rule: quality non-inferior within 5pp before any cost claim

noise_and_power_plan.plan: 4 runs; same model, temperature 0, arm order alternated by task index
noise_and_power_plan.statement: 2 clusters cannot establish a distribution; this run can only contradict or fail to contradict the dev result

cache_order_design.order: arm order alternated by task index
cache_order_design.cache: provider-side cache state is not controllable and is not claimed

stopping_rule: stop after 4 runs or 400k tokens, whichever comes first

holdout_policy.retirement_action: this suite becomes validation; a new one must be frozen before another claim
